::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## What you'll learn
- A genuine 2×2 coupled MIMO plant: shared normal modes, diagonal notches, real cross-coupling.
- Element-by-element recovery — the step before the *joint* modal fit of examples 09–10.
:::

Real suspensions do not move one degree of freedom at a time, and the cross-coupling is
**not** a rescaled copy of the diagonal. A length (POS) drive and a pitch (PIT) drive share
the *same normal modes*, so the honest model is a coupled 2×2 matrix

$$
H(s) = \bigl(M s^2 + C s + K\bigr)^{-1},
\qquad
\begin{bmatrix} y_{\text{POS}} \\ y_{\text{PIT}} \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} H_{11} & H_{12} \\ H_{21} & H_{22} \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} u_{\text{POS}} \\ u_{\text{PIT}} \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Every element shares the normal-mode **poles**; what differs is the **numerator**:
the diagonals carry an *anti-resonance notch* at the partner DoF's mode, while the
off-diagonals are notch-free and set by the coupling. We build that from a modal
expansion (`plant.coupled_suspension`) using representative Advanced-LIGO quad
rigid-body frequencies, then identify the whole matrix one input column at a time.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Modeling note
This is a **simplified, physically-motivated** model — a coupled 2-DoF normal-mode
expansion with a single longitudinal↔pitch coupling — **not** a validated full Advanced-LIGO
suspension state-space model. The mode frequencies are *representative* values from the
aLIGO quad rigid-body modes (longitudinal ≈ 0.43, 1.00, 2.01, 3.42 Hz; pitch ≈ 0.56, 1.31,
2.81 Hz), of which we use the two lowest of each here. Sources:
Aston *et al.*, *Quadruple suspension design for Advanced LIGO*, Class. Quantum Grav. **29**
(2012) 235004 ([DCC P1200056](https://dcc.ligo.org/LIGO-P1200056)); Sauter *et al.*,
*Identification of Resonant Frequencies in LIGO-like Suspension with FEM*, Phys. Rev. D
**109** (2024) 064033 ([arXiv:2306.13755](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13755)).
:::

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Setup — coupled L/P plant from aLIGO modal frequencies"
import sys, pathlib
_p = pathlib.Path.cwd()
for _c in [_p, *_p.parents]:
    for _d in (_c, _c / "docs"):
        if (_d / "sysid_plots.py").exists() and str(_d) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(_d))

import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import sysid_plots as sp
from sysid_campaign import param_sigmas, param_convergence_series

from system_ident.backends.twin import TwinBackend
from system_ident.plant import SuspensionPlant, coupled_suspension
from system_ident.excitation import multisine_from_psd
from system_ident.loop import SysIDLoop
from system_ident.estimators.gml import GMLEstimator
from system_ident.fisher import fisher_matrix
from system_ident.design.pintelon import optimal_excitation, prior_robust_excitation

FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS = 32.0, 8192, 4           # T_fft = 256 s, df ≈ 0.004 Hz
TOTAL = NPERSEG * N_PERIODS / FS
ACT_LIMIT = 1000.0
INPUTS = ["POS", "PIT"]
ELEMS = [("POS", "POS"), ("PIT", "POS"), ("POS", "PIT"), ("PIT", "PIT")]
ECOLOR = {("POS", "POS"): sp.SKY, ("PIT", "PIT"): sp.GOLD,
          ("PIT", "POS"): sp.ROSE, ("POS", "PIT"): sp.GREEN}

# Two lowest aLIGO longitudinal + pitch modes, with damped Qs; genuine L↔P coupling.
LONG = [(0.43, 20.0), (1.00, 30.0)]
PITCH = [(0.56, 18.0), (1.31, 28.0)]
TRUE = coupled_suspension(LONG, PITCH, coupling=0.20, gain=100.0)
PRIOR = coupled_suspension([(f * 1.12, q * 0.8) for f, q in LONG],
                           [(f * 0.88, q * 1.2) for f, q in PITCH],
                           coupling=0.20, gain=120.0)

plant = SuspensionPlant({"POS": TRUE[("POS", "POS")], "PIT": TRUE[("PIT", "PIT")]}, FS)
coupling = {("PIT", "POS"): TRUE[("PIT", "POS")], ("POS", "PIT"): TRUE[("POS", "PIT")]}
exc = {"POS": "C1:EXC_POS", "PIT": "C1:EXC_PIT"}
rsp = {"POS": "C1:RSP_POS", "PIT": "C1:RSP_PIT"}
tw = TwinBackend(plant, {c: d for d, c in exc.items()}, {c: d for d, c in rsp.items()},
                 fs=FS, sensor_asd=2e-3, coupling=coupling)

f_all = np.fft.rfftfreq(NPERSEG, 1 / FS)
band = (f_all >= 0.1) & (f_all <= 5.0); freq = f_all[band]
Pyy, Px_tot = np.ones_like(freq), 1.0
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Run 3 passes, one input column at a time"
est = GMLEstimator()
model = {k: PRIOR[k] for k in ELEMS}
hist = {k: [] for k in ELEMS}
accum = {k: {"w": np.zeros(len(freq)), "wH": np.zeros(len(freq), complex)} for k in ELEMS}
info = {k: np.zeros((PRIOR[k].num.size + PRIOR[k].den.size - 1,) * 2) for k in ELEMS}
col = {j: [] for j in INPUTS}
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
zero = np.zeros(int(round(TOTAL * FS)))

for p in range(3):
    for j in INPUTS:                     # drive column j from its diagonal model
        diag = model[(j, j)]
        Pxx = (prior_robust_excitation(freq, diag, Pyy, Px_tot, 0.5, n_iter=6)
               if p == 0 else optimal_excitation(freq, diag, Pyy, Px_tot, n_iter=6))
        for kk in INPUTS:
            tw.inject(exc[kk], zero, FS)
        drive = multisine_from_psd(Pxx, FS, NPERSEG, N_PERIODS, freq, seed=rng)
        tw.inject(exc[j], drive, FS)
        seg = tw.read([exc[j], rsp["POS"], rsp["PIT"]], TOTAL)
        tw.inject(exc[j], zero, FS)
        col[j].append(dict(**{"pass": p + 1}, drive=seg[exc[j]],
                           resp={i: seg[rsp[i]] for i in INPUTS},
                           peak=float(np.max(np.abs(seg[exc[j]]))),
                           rms=float(np.std(seg[rsp[j]]))))
        for i in INPUTS:
            key = (i, j)
            Hh, He, coh = SysIDLoop._estimate_tf_periodic(seg[exc[j]], seg[rsp[i]],
                                                          FS, NPERSEG, band)
            Hacc, eacc = SysIDLoop._accumulate(accum[key], Hh, He)
            model[key] = est.fit(freq, Hacc, eacc, model[key])
            info[key] = info[key] + fisher_matrix(freq, model[key], Pxx, Pyy, TOTAL)
            cov = np.linalg.inv(info[key])
            hist[key].append(dict(**{"pass": p + 1}, H=Hh, H_err=He, coh=coh,
                mask=np.isfinite(He), H_acc=Hacc, err_acc=eacc, model=model[key],
                cov=cov, frac=SysIDLoop._frac_uncertainty(model[key], cov)))
fit = {k: model[k] for k in ELEMS}
```

## The normal modes — recovered

All four matrix elements share the same poles, so we read the four normal-mode
frequencies off the best-conditioned fits (the diagonals) and compare to truth.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Normal-mode frequencies: prior → fit → true"
# Every element shares the 4 normal modes; the diagonals resolve them best.
mt = sp.modes(TRUE[("POS", "POS")])       # 4 modes, sorted by frequency
mp = sp.modes(PRIOR[("POS", "POS")])
mf = sp.modes(fit[("POS", "POS")])
kind = ["L", "P", "L", "P"]               # which DoF each sorted mode belongs to
rows = []
for n in range(4):
    rows.append([f"mode {n+1} ({kind[n]})", f"{mp[n][0]:.3f}/{mp[n][1]:.0f}",
                 f"{mf[n][0]:.3f}/{mf[n][1]:.1f}", f"{mt[n][0]:.3f}/{mt[n][1]:.0f}"])
sp.param_table(["normal mode", "prior f₀/Q", "fit f₀/Q", "true f₀/Q"], rows,
               caption="Shared normal modes (Hz / Q) — L = longitudinal, P = pitch")
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Normal-mode frequency recovery with CRB error bars"
hpp = hist[("POS", "POS")][-1]
tgt = [f"f0_{n}" for n in range(4)]
sig = param_sigmas(hpp["model"], hpp["cov"], targets=tuple(tgt))
sp.parameter_recovery([
    dict(label=f"f{n+1} [Hz] ({kind[n]})", prior=mp[n][0], fit=mf[n][0],
         true=mt[n][0], sigma=sig[f"f0_{n}"]) for n in range(4)]).show()
```

## Is the drive gentle? — time series (POS driven)

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive (POS) + both outputs, first ~64 s of pass 1"
c0 = col["POS"][0]
t = np.arange(int(64 * FS)) / FS
sp.timeseries(t, [("drive (POS)", c0["drive"], sp.SKY)],
    [("POS motion (direct)", c0["resp"]["POS"], sp.GOLD),
     ("PIT motion (cross-coupling)", c0["resp"]["PIT"], sp.ROSE)],
    titles=["<b>Drive</b> — POS actuator (Schroeder multisine)",
            "<b>Mirror motion</b> — both DoFs respond (genuine coupling)"]).show()
```

## The 2×2 matrix — magnitude, phase, coherence

Note the **notch** between the peaks on the diagonals (`H[POS←POS]`, `H[PIT←PIT]`) and its
*absence* on the off-diagonals — the signature of a genuinely coupled system, not a scaled
diagonal.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Helper: a 2×2 matrix of any per-element quantity"
def matrix(kind_, height=580):
    fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=2, shared_xaxes=True,
        subplot_titles=[f"H[{i}←{j}]" for i in INPUTS for j in INPUTS],
        vertical_spacing=0.12, horizontal_spacing=0.09)
    for r, i in enumerate(INPUTS):
        for c, j in enumerate(INPUTS):
            key = (i, j); h = hist[key][-1]; mask = h["mask"]; lead = (r == 0 and c == 0)
            if kind_ == "coh":
                fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=freq[mask], y=np.asarray(h["coh"])[mask],
                    mode="markers", marker=dict(color=sp.SKY, size=sp.MK_DATA),
                    showlegend=False), row=r + 1, col=c + 1)
                continue
            if kind_ == "mag":
                line_x, fn = freq, (lambda H: np.abs(H))
                meas_y = np.abs(h["H_acc"])[mask]
            else:
                line_x, fn = freq[mask], (lambda H: np.unwrap(np.angle(H[mask])) * 180 / np.pi)
                meas_y = np.unwrap(np.angle(h["H_acc"][mask])) * 180 / np.pi
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=line_x, y=fn(TRUE[key].eval(freq)), mode="lines",
                line=dict(color=sp.SKY, width=2.3), name="true", legendgroup="t",
                showlegend=lead), row=r + 1, col=c + 1)
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=freq[mask], y=meas_y, mode="markers",
                marker=dict(color=sp.GRAY, size=sp.MK_SMALL), name="measured",
                legendgroup="m", showlegend=lead), row=r + 1, col=c + 1)
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=line_x, y=fn(fit[key].eval(freq)), mode="lines",
                line=dict(color=sp.GOLD, width=1.9, dash="dash"), name="ML fit",
                legendgroup="f", showlegend=lead), row=r + 1, col=c + 1)
    ylab = {"mag": "|G(f)|", "phase": "phase [deg]", "coh": "coherence γ²"}[kind_]
    if kind_ == "mag":
        fig.update_yaxes(type="log")
    if kind_ == "coh":
        fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, 1.02])
    else:
        fig.update_yaxes(title_text=ylab, col=1)
    fig.update_xaxes(type="log"); fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Frequency [Hz]", row=2)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text=ylab, col=1)
    return sp.style(fig, height=height)

matrix("mag").show()
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Phase matrix"

```

## Convergence — every normal mode (from the diagonal) + per-element overview

```{python}
#| code-summary: "σᵢ/θᵢ vs pass for the 4 normal modes"
sp.convergence(param_convergence_series(hist[("POS", "POS")],
    [f"f0_{n}" for n in range(4)], [f"f{n+1}" for n in range(4)]),
    target=0.05).show()
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "worst σ/θ vs pass, per element"
sp.convergence([dict(name=f"H[{k[0]}←{k[1]}]", x=[h["pass"] for h in hist[k]],
                     y=[h["frac"] for h in hist[k]], color=ECOLOR[k]) for k in ELEMS],
               target=0.05, ylabel="worst σ/θ per element").show()
```

## Drive-safety margins (per input column)

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Drive peak & RMS vs the actuator limit, per column"
for j in INPUTS:
    sp.saturation([{"pass": c["pass"], "peak": c["peak"], "rms": c["rms"]} for c in col[j]],
                  limit=ACT_LIMIT).show()
```

## Per-element detail

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Helper: bode / residuals / overlay for one element"
def show_elem(key):
    h = hist[key]; mask = h[-1]["mask"]; final = fit[key]
    sp.bode(freq, [
        dict(name="true", H=TRUE[key].eval(freq), color=sp.SKY, width=2.6),
        dict(name="measured (±σ)", H=h[-1]["H_acc"], color=sp.GRAY, mode="markers",
             err=h[-1]["err_acc"], mask=mask),
        dict(name="prior", H=PRIOR[key].eval(freq), color=sp.RED, dash="dot"),
        dict(name="ML fit", H=final.eval(freq), color=sp.GOLD, dash="dash"),
    ], coh=h[-1]["coh"], coh_mask=mask).show()
    resid = ((h[-1]["H_acc"] - final.eval(freq)) / h[-1]["err_acc"]).real
    sp.residuals(freq, resid, mask).show()
    sp.pass_overlay(freq, [dict(meas_mag=np.abs(x["H"]),
        fit_mag=np.abs(x["model"].eval(freq)), mask=x["mask"]) for x in h],
        np.abs(TRUE[key].eval(freq))).show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Shared poles, different zeros
Driving one input column and reading both outputs gives that column of the matrix. Because
all four elements come from the same $(Ms^2+Cs+K)^{-1}$, they share the normal-mode poles —
the diagonals add an anti-resonance **zero** at the partner mode (the notch), the
off-diagonals do not. The reference-based, leakage-free FRF resolves every element, so even
the coupling terms are recovered; the off-diagonals are intrinsically lower-SNR (coupling
sets their level), so they carry the larger residuals.
:::
